report.source_text: There were dense inflammatory adhesions between the anterior gastric wall and the undersurface of the left lobe of the liver, and careful dissection revealed a large amount of purulent fluid which was aspirated and sent for bacterial culture. A moderate amount of fibrinous material adhering the liver surface to the stomach wall was debrided and indicated the abscess had been unroofed. As dissection progressed, an approximately 3 cm white foreign body consistent with a fish bone was removed under direct visualization and sent to pathology (Fig. 3). The stomach was insufflated with air via a nasogastric tube which did not show any obvious leak. The upper abdomen was irrigated, and a drain was placed with the tip in the hepatic abscess cavity and coursing along the anterior wall of the stomach.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Liver abscess secondary to gastric perforation from ingested fish bone foreign body
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old male with no prior medical history presented to the ED with a 5-day history of fever (38.2°C) and headache, accompanied by tachycardia (121 bpm), hypertension (168/101 mmHg), elevated WBC (12,600/mm³), elevated transaminases (AST 48 U/L, ALT 83 U/L), and mild right hemidiaphragm elevation on chest X-ray. He was treated with intravenous fluids and acetaminophen, with normalization of vital signs, and discharged pending blood culture results. Three days after discharge, he returned with right upper quadrant and epigastric tenderness on examination. Laboratory studies showed interval increase in leukocytosis (16,500/mm³), AST (52 U/L), and ALT (105 U/L). Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 5.1 × 7.5 × 3.9 cm heterogeneous hypoattenuating lesion in the left hepatic lobe with rim enhancement and characteristic double target sign, extending to the gastro-hepatic recess near the lesser curvature of the stomach, consistent with hepatic abscess. Laparoscopic exploration revealed dense inflammatory adhesions between the anterior gastric wall and the undersurface of the left lobe of the liver. After careful dissection and unroofing of the abscess, a large amount of purulent fluid was aspirated and cultured. A 3 cm white foreign body consistent with a fish bone was removed under direct visualization. Stomach insufflation via nasogastric tube showed no obvious leak. A drain was placed in the hepatic abscess cavity. Bacterial culture of the purulent fluid grew Streptococcus anginosus and Actinomyces odontolyticus. The postoperative course was noneventful. The patient was discharged with the drain in place and treated with oral Cefdinir and Metronidazole for 1 week. At follow-up, the patient was recovering well without adverse sequelae.
